data.title: Jimmy Kimmel, Disney in talks to renew late-night show for another year
data.description:
Jimmy Kimmel and his employer, Disney-owned ABC, are reportedly in negotiations to extend “Jimmy Kimmel Live” for another year, according to Variety, just days after Page Six said the late-night host was making the current TV season his last.

Kimmel’s current one-year contract is a sharp cut from his previous three-year deal, as late-night audiences decline, advertising dollars dry up, and production costs rise.

Earlier this week, reports circulated that Kimmel’s show would not be renewed after a 24-year run following a tumultuous 12 months that saw the host suspended for comments surrounding Charlie Kirk’s assassination, increased regulatory pressure from the Federal Communications Commission, and his ongoing public feud with President Trump.

A source familiar with the situation told Page Six, “His contract is not getting extended,” a claim an ABC spokesperson swiftly denied.

“This information is inaccurate—any reports about the future of the show at this point are purely speculative.”

Jimmy Kimmel’s current contract ends in May 2027.

data.title: Oracle shook off fears about AI spending, but its stock has now turned south
data.description:
By Barbara Kollmeyer and Hannah Pedone

'Several of Oracle's bear cases were addressed head on' in the latest earnings report, according to an analyst

Oracle won praise from Wall Street analysts after its earnings report.

Analysts say Oracle helped dispel a string of investor concerns with its latest earnings report, and that's being reflected in the stock's momentum.

While there's no doubt that Oracle (ORCL) is growing, a key issue for investors has been the level of spending required to drive that growth. But Piper Sandler analyst Billy Fitzsimmons noted after Thursday's report that the company opted to maintain its forecast for capital expenditures, or money put toward things like data centers and hardware. That's significant because there were fears that management would lift its spending outlook.

Oracle shares were climbing 6% in Friday's premarket action.

"Several of Oracle's bear cases were addressed head on," Fitzsimmons said in his note to clients.

Bernstein analyst Mark Moerdler added that investors' interest in Oracle's stock is high, and those who don't currently own shares are looking "to understand the opportunity and gain confidence the bear concerns are wrong."

To that end, the latest report, he said, boosted "clarity" around a positive investment case for Oracle's stock.

"Oracle is not only executing well but also communicating better, with more details, clarity and increased confidence," he wrote. "The company is also diversifying its customer base while increasing RPO, which does not require meaningful additional cash requirements." RPO refers to remaining performance obligations, or the dollar value of contracted services that have yet to be delivered to customers or booked as revenue.

StoneX analyst Yi Fu Lee wrote in a Friday note that a big takeaway from Oracle's earnings was that Oracle Cloud Infrastructure saw 121% growth from the prior year. "Oracle continues signing large scale AI-related contracts while emphasizing that customer demand still exceeds available supply," he wrote.

Lee said that the report shows that "enterprise AI continues moving beyond experimentation and into production deployment."

JPMorgan analysts pointed to an August quarter that they said eased key worries around data-center delay. Analysts led by Samik Chatterjee noted 850 megawatts of AI computing power were delivered in the quarter, three times what was seen in the May quarter. They also highlighted $30 billion-plus in new AI contracts.

"We got both better in-period execution and future-period bookings than anticipated. Check and check," added Jackson Ader at KeyBanc Capital Markets.

Yet some analysts still had lingering concerns, especially surrounding gross margins, which measure the portion of revenue that a company retains after covering the costs of making its products. Morgan Stanley analyst Sanjit Singh said he wanted to see more stabilization of those margins as well as details on when new data centers will be up and running.

The next major event for Oracle is an analyst day expected to take place in October.

-Barbara Kollmeyer -Hannah Pedone

data.title: Saudi Arabia Shuts Key Crude-Oil Pipeline — WSJ
data.description:
By WSJ Staff

Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry said the East-West pipeline was hit several times Thursday in attacks that caused a number of injuries and led the kingdom to shut it down. The crucial pipeline carries crude from Saudi Arabia's producing heartland on the Persian Gulf to Yanbu on the Red Sea, bypassing the blockage in Hormuz.

Saudi Arabia's oil industry was already reeling. The kingdom's crude-oil production fell to its lowest level in more than three decades last month, dropping by 2.3 million barrels a day to 6 million barrels a day in August, the International Energy Agency said in a report Friday. Saudi Arabia produced around 9.4 million barrels a day on average last year.

data.title: Oracle, Kroger, Adobe, and More Stocks That Explain Today's Market — Barrons.com
data.description:
By George Glover and Mariapaula Gonzalez

Stocks rose Friday after data showed inflation slightly topped Wall Street's expectations in August, increasing the odds of a Federal Reserve rate hike at its meeting next week.

Oracle rose 2.1% after the software giant beat analysts' earnings target for its fiscal first quarter. The results also helped ease some concerns about Oracle's reliance on OpenAI.

Oracle's earnings boosted other artificial-intelligence stocks. Advanced Micro Devices, Qualcomm, Corning, and Intel all traded higher. Micron, however, dipped 0.2%.

Adobe dipped 0.3%. The web design tool developer's third-quarter earnings topped Wall Street's expectations, but that wasn't enough to revive sentiment for a stock that has been battered by AI worries.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise was the best-performing stock in the S&P 500.

Kroger gained 3.8%. The grocery giant lowered its forecast for same-store sales growth for the fiscal year to between 0.2% and 0.8%, down from a previous range of 1% and 2%. The tighter guidance stemmed from a hit to pharmacy revenue caused by Medicare drug price cuts under the Inflation Reduction Act. Kroger also noted that the cyclospora outbreak affecting fresh produce reduced total same-store sales growth.

Copart rose 0.4% after the online car seller said it had agreed to buy rival ACV in a deal with an implied equity value of about $1.9 billion, which helped investors to shrug off a fourth-quarter earnings miss.

RH gained 3.1% after the furniture retailer smashed analysts' second-quarter profit estimates and said that recent brand expansion could double its overall total addressable market.

data.title: U.S. Sale-Leaseback Activity Rises — Market Talk
data.description: Sale leasebacks, or transactions in which a business sells a property and immediately rents it back, totaled about $4.57 billion across the U.S. during this year's second quarter, nearly 60% more than in the same period of last year, according to SLB Capital Advisors, which specializes in such deals. The number of transactions increased about 14%, to 178. "Paired with a strong 1Q, the first half of 2026 reflects sustained momentum and the most active start to a year since 2022," the New York firm says. The industrial sector represented the largest share, or 42%, of sale leasebacks during the latest quarter, SLB's data shows. Real estate investment trust Vici Properties had the largest deal in the period with its acquisition of seven casino locations from Golden Entertainment for $1.16 billion. (luis.garcia@wsj.com)

data.title: Canada Auto Workers' Talks With Stellantis Hit Impasse Over Future of Ontario Factory, Union Says
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--The union representing Canada's automotive workers said talks on a new labor deal with Stellantis have stalled over the company's plans for a factory that has been idle for two years.

Stellantis executives, during bargaining, reiterated the company's plan to sell its factory in Brampton, Ontario, Unifor said. The car maker has an interested buyer in Roshel, a Canadian-based producer of smart-armored vehicles, and the two parties have signed a memorandum of understanding, the union said.

Stellantis confirmed it has been in negotiations with Roshel.

"The persistence of the company's proposal to close and sell the Brampton plant has hindered the bargaining process," Unifor said, adding that its talks with Stellantis have reached an impasse. The union represents over 9,000 of the company's employees.

A Stellantis spokeswoman said Roshel represents the best option to restoring operations at its Brampton assembly plant, "preserving the site's strategic role in Canada's advanced manufacturing sector and helping to avoid a prolonged period of inactivity." She had no further comment, citing collective-bargaining talks with Unifor.

Representatives for Roshel weren't immediately available for comment.

Unifor said the current collective agreement with Stellantis expires on Sept. 20.

data.title: Live cattle futures higher on strengthening cash market, short covering
data.description:
Chicago Mercantile Exchange live and feeder cattle futures ended higher on Friday on support from a strengthening cattle market and a bout of short covering ahead of the weekend in a bounce off of last week's lows.

CME October live cattle settled 1.85 cents higher to 219.675 cents per pound. CME October feeder cattle rose 4.95 cents to 332.5 cents per pound.

Boxed beef prices have been relatively resilient, though traders are continuing to assess consumer demand for beef, which is typically one of the priciest proteins available at stores and restaurants.

Inflation and high gas prices in particular have led to concerns that consumers will trade down from beef to cheaper proteins to save money.

"With gas prices still elevated, that's a concern moving forward here," said Austin Schroeder, analyst at Brugler Marketing.

Choice cuts of boxed beef were down $2.41 to $375.96 per hundredweight (cwt) on Friday, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture. Select cuts rose $1.60 to $353.67 per hundredweight.

The first horse in the United States to be infected with New World screwworm has been detected in southern Texas near the Mexican border, data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture showed.

The case of the flesh-eating parasite was confirmed on Wednesday in Presidio County, USDA's website showed, after months of infestation of U.S. cattle that has raised alarms about how to control the spread of the pest.

The re-opening of the U.S.-Mexico border to cattle imports has largely already been factored into the market, traders said. The number of cattle moving through the open port has been relatively small.

In pork, the most actively traded October lean hog contract (LHV26) closed 1.625 cents lower at 81.525 cents per pound.

The USDA reported wholesale pork carcass values at $92.11, up 30 cents from the previous day.

data.title: CBOT wheat lower as traders assess Black Sea conflict
data.description:
Chicago Board of Trade wheat futures fell as traders focused on the impacts of Russia's war on Ukraine, with renewed diplomatic moves to end the war adding bearishness.

  • Attacks on the city of Dnipro that damaged a vegetable oil factory of U.S. agrifood group Bunge kept attention on continuing disruption to the massive Black Sea grain trade.

  • Commerzbank raised its year-end wheat price forecasts, citing the ongoing attacks by Russia and Ukraine on each other's ports.

  • Russia's seaborne grain exports fell by 61.9% year-on-year in August to 2.0 million metric tons, mainly due to a decline in shipments through the Azov-Black Sea basin, according to shipping data from industry sources released on Friday.

  • Russia and Ukraine have sharply escalated attacks on each other's shipping in recent weeks. Following drone strikes, Russian authorities suspended navigation in the Sea of Azov in early July, while an August 12 attack halted loading operations at key terminals at Novorossiysk, Russia's largest Black Sea port.

  • Exports via Azov and Black Sea ports declined by 73.1% year-on-year in August to 1.3 million tons, the data showed.

  • CBOT December soft red winter wheat (WZ26) settled 12-1/2 cents lower to $7.41-1/4 per bushel.

  • Kansas City December hard red winter wheat (KWZ26) settled 20-1/4 cents lower to $7.98-1/2 per bushel.

  • Minneapolis December wheat (MWEZ26) settled 17-1/2 cents lower to $7.45 per bushel.

data.title: Raw sugar slides off 16-month peak, arabica near 10-week low as ICE stocks set to rise
data.description:
Raw sugar futures slid off their 16-month peaks on Friday, closing the week with only marginal gains, while arabica coffee hovered near 10-week lows amid signs that ICE exchange stocks are set to rise.

SUGAR

* Raw sugar settled down 0.58 cent, or 3.1%, at 18.15 cents per lb, after hitting a 16-month peak of 18.88 cents on Thursday. The market gained 0.4% weekly.

* The recent run up in sugar has been driven by tight supplies in India, Thailand and Europe, as well as strength in energy markets, which can encourage more use of cane to make the biofuel ethanol rather than sugar.

* Oil prices fell on Friday but remained on track to close above $100 a barrel for the first time in nearly 4 months.

* Sugar production in Thailand, the world's second-largest exporter of the commodity after Brazil, is expected to fall 12.5% to 10.5 million metric tons in the 2026/27 season, an industry official said.

* Rains have hampered harvest in Brazil this week, and forecast looks mixed ahead.

* White sugar fell 2.8% to $523.10 a ton.

COFFEE

* Arabica coffee settled down 2.45 cents, or 0.9%, at $2.857 per lb, after setting a 10-week low of $2.8210 on Thursday. The market lost 3.3% in the week.

* Traders are planning to deliver significant volumes of arabica coffee from the world's biggest producer Brazil to ICE exchange warehouses, where stocks have sunk to 26-year lows and driven up prices, dealers, brokers and analysts with knowledge of the matter said.

* Top grower Brazil exported a record volume of green coffee for August, shipping 3.82 million bags, a 31.7% jump compared with last year, industry group Cecafe said.

* This year's harvest in Brazil is now nearly complete and the focus was switching to prospects for the 2027 crop, which is off to a good start with ample rains favouring flowering.

* "The market may be short term oversold, but it has also broken below a two month trading range, and that projects to 240.85, another 40 cents lower from here," said broker ADMIS.

* Robusta coffee fell 0.8% to $3,525 a ton, although posting a 3% gain on the week.

COCOA

* London cocoa ​​settled down £14, or 0.3%, to £4,330 per ton. It lost 4% on the week.

* The market is consolidating after hitting a near one-year high earlier this month.

* ADMIS noted that top growers Ivory Coast and parts of Ghana have received some timely rainfall in recent days.

* New York cocoa was little changed at $5,961 a ton. The market lost 4% weekly.

data.title: Goldman continues to see net upside risk to $4,900/oz end-2026 gold forecast
data.description:
Goldman Sachs continues to see upside potential to its forecast for gold price to reach $4,900 an ounce by the end of 2026, although it expects price swings to remain high, the bank said in a note on Friday.

Goldman's fair-value forecast of $4,900/oz by end-2026 assumes central banks continue buying gold at a strong pace and that investor demand for gold-backed ETFs recovers as the U.S. Federal Reserve keeps interest rates unchanged in 2026.

Highlights from the note:

  • The forecast does not account for the recent surge in demand for gold call options

  • If ETF inflows pick up and current elevated call option positioning persists, dealer hedging could mechanically amplify the rally and drive gold prices above Goldman's forecast

  • A renewed rise in expectations that the Fed will increase interest rates could trigger a selloff

  • "With rate-sensitive ETF holders net selling into higher rates, gold prices could then reach $4,440/oz by end-2026 — materially below our base-case of $4,900."

data.title: Drydocks World and Cochin Shipyard form JV to strengthen India's ship repair industry
data.description:
New Delhi, Sept. 11 -- Drydocks World, a DP World company, and Cochin Shipyard Ltd (CSL) have formed a 50:50 joint venture to operate and expand the International Ship Repair Facility (ISRF) in Kochi, the two companies said in a joint statement on Friday.

Dubai-headquartered Drydocks World and CSL will each hold a 50% stake in the joint venture, with initial capital funded through equity contributions from both parties. Financial details of the joint venture were not disclosed.

The joint venture will consolidate and expand the existing facility to service a wider range of vessels and meet the requirements of Indian, regional and international customers. The partnership will also create opportunities across ship repair, engineering, fabrication and allied maritime services in Kerala.

The agreement formalizes a partnership first outlined in a memorandum of understanding signed by the companies during India Maritime Week 2025 to explore collaboration in ship repair and allied maritime services. The new venture marks the establishment of what the companies described as a first-of-its-kind public-private partnership in India's ship-repair sector.

The partnership combines CSL's established shipbuilding and repair capabilities, engineering expertise and skilled workforce with Drydocks World's global experience in high-end vessel repair and maintenance, major conversions, and offshore engineering, procurement and construction (EPC).

Strategically located along major international shipping routes, the ISRF features a state-of-the-art ship lift system and modern docking facilities capable of servicing a wide range of vessels.

"Anchored at the International Ship Repair Facility in Kochi, this partnership will catalyse a thriving repair cluster, attract international fleets, generate high-skilled employment, and advance the vision of Maritime India 2030 and Amrit Kaal 2047," Jose V J, chairman and managing director, Cochin Shipyard, said in the statement.

The partnership is also intended to strengthen Kerala's maritime-services ecosystem and India's broader maritime competitiveness.

"This joint venture is a significant step in strengthening India's ship repair ecosystem and a major opportunity for Kerala to emerge as a leading maritime services hub.the partnership will create new capacity, skills and economic opportunities for Kerala, while enhancing India's maritime competitiveness," Union Minister of Ports, Shipping and Waterways Sarbananda Sonowal said.

"It supports our vision under Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047 to build a self-reliant and globally competitive maritime sector," he added.

"By combining India's growing maritime potential with the UAE's global experience, collaborations such as this can support more efficient ship repair services, strengthen maritime connectivity and contribute to the continued growth of trade and commerce between our two countries," said Oman Sharaf Alhashimi, assistant foreign minister for advanced science and technology, the United Arab Emirates.

The agreement was signed by Captain Rado Antolovic, chief executive, Drydocks World, and Jose V. on the sidelines of the Brics summit in New Delhi, in the presence of Sonowal and Alhashimi. data.title: Wall Street jumps, oil lower ahead of Fed vote next week
data.description:
Key points:
  • Brent hits $109 a barrel, before easing to below $104
  • US Treasury yields hit multi-year highs, now steady
  • US stocks higher, still set for weekly decline
  • US CPI accelerates ahead of Fed meeting next week

By Pete Schroeder

Wall Street ticked up on Friday after a volatile, mostly down week and oil prices dipped after a week-long surge in which Gulf tensions and inflation concerns weighed on markets.

Oil prices retreated from a four-month high on Friday, but accelerating U.S. consumer inflation boosted expectations for an interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve next week, keeping bond yields elevated.

All three major U.S. indices were higher on Friday but still on track for a weekly loss. The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 1.13%, the S&P 500 gained 1.03% and the Nasdaq Composite was up 1.15%.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe EURONEXT:IACWI rose 5.66 points, or 0.50%.

TRADERS AWAIT FED STATEMENT

The Consumer Price Index increased 0.4% last month after edging up 0.1% in July, the U.S. Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said.

Traders were quick to add to bets for a rate hike from the Fed at its two-day meeting next week. Markets now see about an 85% chance of a quarter-point hike, compared with around 67% prior to the data. The Fed will release its latest policy statement on Wednesday, followed by a press conference with Chairman Kevin Warsh.

"Thus far, the Fed has simply stared at inflation with its withering gaze. (Friday's) report will probably change that," said Shawn Snyder, economic strategist at Potomac Fund Management. "It may not be enough to definitively push the Fed to hike rates at its September meeting, but with oil prices hovering around $100 a barrel, it is hard to envision the inflation outlook getting much better in the near term."

Brent crude hit a four-month high of $109.97 a barrel on Friday after a 6% jump the day before, but it soon ran into selling pressure and was last down about 2.9% at $104.49. It was still set for a weekly rise of over 8%.

Oil flows remained restricted through the Strait of Hormuz as the United States and Iran traded attacks, although prices have fallen since the Financial Times reported that foreign ministers in the Middle East were trying to work out a temporary deal to manage shipping through the waterway.

Markets are still pricing in the risk of a protracted war. Comments by President Donald Trump that the war could last beyond the November midterm elections have not helped, with bond yields surging globally on heightened inflation fears.

The benchmark 10-year Treasury yield was slightly higher on Friday at 4.96%, helped by retreating oil prices. It briefly touched its highest in almost three years at 4.9915% immediately after the inflation data.

The U.S. dollar was flat, having gained 0.4% on Thursday against its major peers. It was steady on Friday at 99.1.

Gold rose 0.8% to $4,350 an ounce after dropping nearly 2% on Thursday. (GOL/)

data.title: Canada Auto Workers' Talks With Stellantis Hit Impasse Over Future of Ontario Factory, Union Says
data.description:
By Paul Vieira

OTTAWA--The union representing Canada's automotive workers said talks on a new labor deal with Stellantis have stalled over the company's plans for a factory that has been idle for two years.

Stellantis executives, during bargaining, reiterated the company's plan to sell its factory in Brampton, Ontario, Unifor said. The car maker has an interested buyer in Roshel, a Canadian-based producer of smart-armored vehicles, and the two parties have signed a memorandum of understanding, the union said.

Stellantis confirmed it has been in negotiations with Roshel.

"The persistence of the company's proposal to close and sell the Brampton plant has hindered the bargaining process," Unifor said, adding that its talks with Stellantis have reached an impasse. The union represents over 9,000 of the company's employees.

A Stellantis spokeswoman said Roshel represents the best option to restoring operations at its Brampton assembly plant, "preserving the site's strategic role in Canada's advanced manufacturing sector and helping to avoid a prolonged period of inactivity." She had no further comment, citing collective-bargaining talks with Unifor.

Representatives for Roshel weren't immediately available for comment.

Unifor said the current collective agreement with Stellantis expires on Sept. 20.

data.title: Roblox expands tools to help creators build, distribute games
data.description:
Roblox plans to let creators distribute their games as standalone apps across mobile, PC and consoles, the company said at its developers conference on Friday, as it seeks to make games easier to access beyond the Roblox app.

The gaming platform will provide the underlying technology and services for the standalone apps. By the end of the year, players will also be able to join games in Chrome from a game's Experience Details page without downloading an app, with additional browsers to follow.

Roblox will also allow creators to combine online and offline modes in one game, enabling single-player campaigns and play without a network connection.

The company is also expanding its AI tools for game creation, including Build, Scene Generator and new non-player character features.

Roblox introduced Build in July, allowing users to create, test and publish a playable game from a text prompt within its app. The company said users have published about 9,000 games with Build, and 71% of those who created a game with the tool had not previously used Roblox Studio.

Scene Generator, due later this year, will let creators use a text prompt and reference image to create a functional game layout. Roblox also plans to add non-player characters that can playtest games.

data.title: Roblox Unveils New Ways to Play, Build, and Grow at the Roblox Developers Conference (RDC)
data.description:
Roblox Corporation (NYSE: RBLX) today announced new innovations at its 12th annual Roblox Developers Conference (RDC), an invite-only event for Roblox’s creator community of developers, artists, designers, brands, and influencers. Celebrating 20 years of platform innovation alongside its community, the company unveiled updates that aim to expand play, give creators the game engine and AI tools to build things that weren’t possible before, and usher in the next chapter of growth for creators.

Play: New Ways to Connect, Communicate and Enjoy Games

Last quarter alone, players spent 29 billion hours on Roblox1, across more than 180 countries. Today, Roblox shared updates designed to let players join games anywhere, on any device or platform; stay connected between sessions; and play new formats and gameplay styles:

  • Play Roblox Everywhere: Roblox Everywhere will help creators reach audiences where they already are. Soon, creators will have the option to make their games available as standalone apps across mobile, PC, and consoles, with Roblox powering the technology and services underneath.

  • Play on the Web: By the end of this year, players will be able to join a game in-browser on Chrome (additional browsers to follow) from a game’s Experience Details Page, with no app or install required. A shared link, anywhere on the web, becomes a direct path from discovery to play.

  • Play Offline: Players can keep playing, even if they’re in the air or service is spotty. Creators will be able to combine online and offline modes in one game, opening up single-player campaigns and sessions away from a network.

  • Play New Kinds of Games: Roblox is best known for 3D multiplayer worlds, but some of the most-played games in the world are 2D and puzzle games. Roblox is expanding its engine capabilities to support 2D games with a new orthographic camera, animated image containers, and direct sprite-sheet import. New UI features, including blur, text shadows, and improved gradients, will enhance the look and feel for games, and a new notification system will support turn-based, asynchronous multiplayer games.

  • Stay Connected Between Games: The new Friends chat tab follows players across games, so friends can coordinate and move into a new game together, and newly released voice typing lets players talk rather than type while playing.

Build: Expanding the Game Engine and AI Creation

Roblox has built what is effectively a cloud operating system for gaming and is now building an AI creation layer on top of it: not a single tool or model, but a system built for the complexity of games.

  • Build Expansion: Build, a tab in the Roblox app that lets anyone create and publish a game just by prompting, is now expanding to public alpha in Serbia and Singapore.2 Following the alpha launch in New Zealand this summer, creators have used Build to publish approximately 9,000 games, and 71% of the thousands of users who’ve created a game with Build had never used Roblox Studio before.3 Roblox is also adding new tools to give creators more control, including a new asset library, desktop access, and iterative control. Today, creators can quickly review analytics and add monetization, and soon they’ll also be able to launch ads for their games from their phones.

  • Scene Generator: Arriving later this year, Scene Generator will bring prompt-to-scene functionality to both Build and Studio, with greater creator control available in Studio. Creators supply a text prompt and a reference image, and Scene Generator returns a fully functional layout they can then refine in Studio.

  • NPC Capabilities: Roblox is expanding what NPCs can do on Roblox with two new behaviors by year-end, including NPCs that playtest.

Grow: A New Chapter for Creator Monetization and Game Discovery

Since launching DevEx in 2013, creators have earned more than $5 billion on Roblox. In the past 12 months, creators have earned approximately $1.7 billion.4 Today, Roblox introduced the next evolution in creator earnings on the platform.

  • Roblox Wallet: A financial account built to scale with creator businesses, Wallet lets creators earn directly in real currency, get paid automatically each business day, and move funds to other Roblox accounts or an external account, with richer earnings analytics in Creator Hub. Wallet is an account provided through Roblox’s financial partner5 and is a foundation for helping independent creators grow into business owners. Roblox Wallet rolls out later this year to eligible U.S.-based independent creators 18 and older and will begin expanding globally next year.

  • Roblox Card: Connected to Roblox Wallet, Roblox Card lets creators spend their available balance anywhere the card is accepted. Roblox Card will begin rolling out next year.

Great games should be easy to find, whether on the Roblox homepage, in Moments, or on any browser or device.

  • Moments: The Moments tab, where players watch gameplay videos and click to play, is now fully available in the United States.2 Coming soon, gameplay preview videos from Experience Details Pages will start appearing in Moments, players will be able to tap any avatar to buy the items shown, and Build games will be playable in the tab.

  • Discovery Ranking: Roblox’s discovery ranking system now optimizes for both younger players, who tend to engage best with shorter-form games, and older players, who are drawn to deeper games they return to over time, looking beyond the first week to the first 28 days and beyond. Roblox is also testing optimizing for direct growth, measured by how many new players a game brings to the platform.

For more information and details on additional products announced at RDC, please visit the Roblox Newsroom.

About Roblox

Roblox is an immersive gaming and creation platform that offers people millions of ways to be together, inviting its community to explore, create, and share endless unique experiences. Roblox’s vision is to reimagine the way people come together—in a world that’s safe, civil, and optimistic. To achieve this vision, Roblox is building an innovative company that, together with the community, has the ability to strengthen the social fabric and support economic growth for people around the world. data.title: House of the Week: A Modern Farmhouse on an Oregon Island — WSJ
data.description:
By Nancy Keates

It was a red pickup truck that inspired Julie and Peter Stott to buy a home on Sauvie Island, a strip of land along the Columbia River about 10 miles northwest of downtown Portland, Ore.

Peter, 82, had long wanted to own a 1950 Chevy pickup, pointing one out every time he saw it on the road. Julie, 74, bought him the classic two-door, five-window truck for his 70th birthday.

"We decided we needed a farm to go along with it," says Peter, an entrepreneur and trucking executive. He once owned a 4,000-acre ranch in Eastern Oregon and missed the acreage. Julie, an interior architect, grew up going to her family's farm near Astoria, Ore.

"The idea of getting a farm wasn't abhorrent to me," she says.

The renovation

The couple, who were living in Portland at the time, paid $1.1 million in 2017 for the farm, which included a run-down home, a barn and cornfields. The land was littered with old appliances and the house had small windows and low ceilings.

They tore down the buildings and redid the landscaping, spending roughly $8 million on a modern farmhouse house and cedar-clad barn, finishing the project in 2022.

Can't-miss features

The new house has a wide front porch and large picture windows that frame views of Mount Hood and the Oregon Coast Range.

Designed for entertainment, the barn features large roll-up doors and a spiral staircase leading to a craft room.

The grounds include flower gardens, raised vegetable beds, a pumpkin patch, an apple and pear orchard, a chicken coop and a swimming pool with an outdoor kitchen and a pool house. Thousands of migrating birds including egrets, cranes, ducks and geese visit the property for a few months every winter.

Reason for selling?

The couple are planning to make their primary residence Richmond, Va., to be closer to their daughter and four children.

What they'll miss

Peter will miss driving across the Sauvie Island Bridge on his way home from work: "Your whole attitude about the day changes," he says.

Julie will miss walking her golden retrievers on the mile-long track around the fields, listening to the crickets, frogs and coyotes, and watching the sun rise and set on opposite sides of the house. "It's a calming place," she says.

What they won't miss

Peter says he won't miss the commute to his Portland office.

Market snapshot

In the first seven months of 2026, the median sale price for a Portland single-family home priced over $3 million rose 2.8% year-over-year to $4.22 million, according to Windermere Realty Trust agents Matt Mahaffy and Sue Sullivan.

data.title: AI Is Creating New Trust Problems Between Colleagues — WSJ
data.description:
By Tessa West

As generative AI has swept into the workplace, much of the debate has focused on how it will shape the future: Will it make us more productive? Eliminate jobs? Transform the nature of work itself?

Those questions may take years to answer. But one consequence is already becoming clear: Artificial intelligence is creating a trust problem among colleagues at work.

We don't know what the rules around AI use are, for instance, so we often can't tell whether our colleagues are breaking them. We don't necessarily believe them when they say they aren't using AI. And we judge them harshly when we suspect they are, even as we conceal our own use.

In other words, AI isn't just changing how we work. It's changing how we relate to-and trust-the people we work with. That distrust threatens to undermine the teamwork and productivity gains that AI is supposed to deliver.

Here are some of the biggest social minefields AI is creating, and what organizations can do about them.

No rules or norms

Generative AI is being incorporated into the workplace at a rapid pace, as fast as the personal computer and faster than the internet was. That said, most organizations lack rules and policies around how employees are supposed to use AI. We not only don't know what's technically allowed-which tasks we can outsource to AI, get a little help with, or get punished for if someone detects even a trace of it-but also, what our bosses, employees and teammates are actually doing.

What's more, even when there are rules, many companies have norms that counter them. One study of 30,000 employees found that about 40% of people used AI at work even when they aren't supposed to.

Take Sara and her colleague Scott. Sara may not care if Scott in the cubicle next to her is using AI to write his reports. But she might care if he's outsourcing his part of a team project to it, leaving her feeling uncertain about his ability to present his work in front of a client next week. Maybe he's cheating. Or maybe he's just super tech savvy and enough of an expert that outsourcing the work is just fine. Sara's not sure what she's supposed to make of Scott's behavior, and she certainly doesn't feel comfortable confronting him, not knowing what the company norms are.

We hide our AI use

There is a good chance that even if Sara did confront Scott, he'll deny at least some of it.

KPMG found that among 48,000 employees, about 57% admitted to trying to pass AI content off as their own. And that is because despite its ubiquity, there is a very strong bias against using it. We label those who outsource their work to AI as lazier and less moral, and we think they value their work less than those who don't.

If you think a work email or text was written with the help of AI, you see it as less genuine than those written presumably by a person, and the writer as less competent. If we think people we're interacting with are using AI to autofill their texts with "smart replies" ("I hope you're doing...really well today!"), we see them as less cooperative and more dominant, and we like them less than if we think they finished those sentences on their own.

Yes, this makes us all hypocrites. We have no problem using AI ourselves to complete tasks faster and help navigate social encounters. But once someone's work is labeled as AI-generated, the negative social judgments will follow.

Sara's not just worried that Scott can't perform in front of a client, she might also think he's incompetent and not very motivated to do his job. She thinks he's cheating by using AI. And unless she confronts him, these judgments will live in her mind unchallenged. We avoid confrontation at work at the best of times when we have clear rules and norms to guide us. It's easy to imagine how quickly a workplace relationship can sour over something as simple as: Did they use AI to make that?

People are bad at detecting AI

After living in a world saturated with AI content, most of us are pretty confident that we can detect the signs of AI in emails, text messages, images and reports. If Sara suspects Scott of using AI, she probably has a good reason for it.

Except she doesn't: Despite all of this exposure, we're no better than chance at detecting AI content-between 50% and 54% on average. Detecting AI is like trying to detect lies: In most cases, there is no single signature that gives AI away, aside from hallucinations. Instead, people rely on the wrong cues, such as how impersonal, monotonous, or how long an email is, in deciding whether AI played a role.

Sara's judgments of Scott are based on a coin flip, and one she doesn't know she's made. She just knows she resents Scott for using AI.

The workplace is full of Scotts and Saras-people who are judging one another's emails and work based on their theories of what AI content ought to look like and whether it was used appropriately. Sara's next step might be to ask Scott to step down from his presentation, leaving Scott in the dark as to why. Or, more likely (remember our aversion for confrontation), she may simply harbor simmering resentment, poisoning their working relationship.

What companies can do

What is the best way for organizations to approach the communication and trust issues that AI can create? Here are some tips.

  • Create groups that discuss how people are using AI, beyond what it was brought in for. When organizations roll out a new AI technology, they focus on how it will affect their performance on the specific tasks it was brought in for. They rarely focus on how else it's being used, appropriate or not.

Groups can be formed, made up of people from different backgrounds and levels of expertise, who represent the diverse ways AI is being used at the company. At the same time, the company should ask employees-anonymously-how they are using AI that may go beyond the company rules.

That survey allows companies to get a clearer picture of how AI is actually being used, rather than leaving employees to guess what their colleagues are doing and whether everyone is playing by the same rules. After all, ignorance breeds suspicion. If everyone assumes other people are secretly using AI in ways they are not supposed to, you get exactly the Sara/Scott problem.

The survey also helps management understand why people are violating the rules, which lets them address underlying problems instead of treating every violation as evidence that an employee is lazy or dishonest. For example, if people are uploading company materials into AI to create reports, violating data-privacy rules, it could be because they are understaffed and won't get through their workload without doing so. Or if people are using AI to tackle an assignment, it could be because they lack skills or training for the task, but can't or won't admit it.

  • Develop clear norms around AI. When organizations base their AI rules and policies around the realities of the workplace-which the survey can help determine-it's much easier to develop clear company norms that aren't violating these rules. The company should have a guidebook that contains a list of workplace situations in which there might be a need, or temptation, to use AI. These situations should make it clear what the black, white and gray areas are.

Shared norms take some of the guesswork, and suspicion, out of AI use: Employees know what their colleagues are permitted to do, what they are expected to disclose, and when an AI-assisted piece of work can be treated just like any other. Sara doesn't need to decide for herself whether Scott is cheating, nor should Scott wonder whether he needs to conceal it. The organization has already established which uses are acceptable.

  • Keep everyone informed about the state of AI use at the company. Companies regularly create quarterly or yearly reports on the state of the company and workplace attitudes. The state of AI use should be included in these reports.

Transparency interrupts the vicious cycle where people think AI use is shameful, so they hide it; that secrecy makes everyone suspicious of everyone else, which only makes AI use seem even more shameful. You couldn't get a better recipe for creating a sour, distrusting workplace.

Clear rules and clear norms won't eliminate every conflict over AI. But by taking the behavior out of the shadows, organizations can replace that toxic suspicion with something more conducive to trust: a shared understanding of what everyone is doing and why.

data.title: AXSM Jumps 6% As Mizuho Calls Auvelity’s Alzheimer’s Launch A ‘Strong Start’
data.description:
Key points:
  • First approved in 2022 as an oral treatment for major depression in adults, Auvelity won a second U.S. clearance in April 2026 for agitation linked to Alzheimer’s dementia.
  • Management has said peak annual sales for Auvelity could reach $8 billion, split roughly evenly between depression and Alzheimer’s agitation.
  • COO Mark Jacobson recently highlighted that Auvelity has no boxed warning for higher death risk in people with dementia, a label that limits the only other approved branded option.

Shares of Axsome Therapeutics (AXSM) rose 6% on Friday after Mizuho analyst Graig Suvannavejh said August prescription data pointed to a strong start for the drug’s newest use.

Citing Bloomberg Symphony figures for the 30-milligram starter dose used when doctors begin treatment, he said new prescriptions rose 32% from July, and total prescriptions rose 34%. The stock is now on track to clock its best day since late July, if gains hold.

“While still early days in the launch, this appears highly indicative of a strong start for Auvelity in ADA,” he wrote. Suvannavejh rates the stock ‘Outperform’ with a $316 price target, implying a potential upside of about 50% from the stock’s last closing price.

Why The New Use Matters

Auvelity is Axsome’s main product. First approved in 2022 as an oral treatment for major depression in adults, it won a second U.S. clearance in April 2026 for agitation linked to Alzheimer’s dementia — the first non-antipsychotic approved for that condition. Axsome began selling into the new indication in June.

The Alzheimer’s launch is central to the company’s finances. Auvelity generated $180.3 million in second-quarter sales, up 51% from a year earlier, and made up most of Axsome’s $218.4 million in product revenue. Management has said peak annual sales could reach $8 billion, split roughly evenly between depression and Alzheimer’s agitation.

Axsome also sells Sunosi for excessive daytime sleepiness tied to narcolepsy or sleep apnea, and Symbravo for acute migraine. Both add sales but remain far smaller than Auvelity.

What Management Is Seeing

At Cantor Fitzgerald’s conference on Thursday, executives said early doctor feedback matches the trial data: agitation eases quickly, and the drug is well tolerated in a frail group.

COO Mark Jacobson highlighted that Auvelity has no boxed warning for higher death risk in people with dementia, a label that limits the only other approved branded option, an antipsychotic. That difference, he said, is already generating interest, with the commercial impact expected to build through year-end.

CFO Nick Pizzie said new prescriptions for patients 65 and older rose 126% after the Alzheimer’s launch. That older Medicare group was about 19% of new starts before approval and is now more than 30%. Most early use is coming from community doctors; nursing homes take longer to bring online, he added.

What Investors Will Watch Next

The next test for AXSM is whether the August jump in starter doses turns into ongoing use of the full maintenance dose and shows up in third-quarter results, expected in early November. Later this year, Axsome is also due to report late-stage data on solriamfetol — Sunosi’s active ingredient — in binge-eating disorder. It has also started a late-stage study of Auvelity’s compound as a smoking-cessation treatment. A separate narcolepsy candidate, AXS-12, has an FDA decision date of May 1, 2027.

How Did AXSM Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around AXSM stock jumped from ‘neutral’ to ‘bullish’ over the past 24 hours, while message volume rose from ‘normal’ to ‘high’ levels.

AXSM stock has gained 22% year-to-date.
